title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages): X is a space stratified by a finite poset I, with strata X_i^*. For a 'band' (a convex subset) K of I, X_K is the union of the strata indexed by K. Choosing compatible tubular neighbourhoods T_i of the strata, one 'unfolds' (déploie) X. Σ_K denotes X_K with the open tubes of the lower boundary strata removed. It is a manifold with corners, the 'deployed' piece over K. For a flag d = (i_0 < ... < i_k) in I, Σ_d is the corresponding corner stratum, morally the iterated tube boundary. The previous page fixes disjoint bands J < L, a band I' in which J is an ideal and L a coideal, and J' = I' \ L, so J ⊂ J' ⊂ I'.

(75) The tubular neighbourhood of Σ_J inside Σ_{I'} is Σ_{I'} ∩ ⋃_{j∈J} T_j. He first writes the same formula with the union over the closure J̄, then notes 'mais en général c'est différent'.

(76) Its boundary Ṫ_{Σ_J,Σ_{I'}} is claimed to be the colimit of the corner pieces Σ_d. The colimit runs over flags d ∈ Drap(I') whose initial terms lie in J and whose final terms lie in I'\J, glued along the face/corner inclusions. In the margin this is identified with Σ^♮_{J,I'\J}.

(77) For a coideal L (the transcribed 'L = I'\J' is probably 'L ⊂ I'\J, L ≠ ∅'), he defines Σ^♮_{J,L}. It is the part of the tube boundary of Σ_J that avoids the open tubes of the intermediate strata J'\J. Equivalently it is Ṫ_{Σ_J,Σ_{I'}} ∩ Σ_L, where Σ_L = Σ_{I'} \ (Σ_{I'} ∩ T̊_{J'}).

(78) 'Sauf erreur', Σ^♮_{J,L} is the colimit of Σ_d over flags in J ∪ L that split as (j_1..j_p | l_1..l_q). This splitting is made explicit as (80) on the next page.

(79) This gives a correspondence Σ_J ← Σ^♮_{J,L} ↪ Σ_L:
- the right arrow is the canonical inclusion;
- the left arrow is the tube projection (retraction).

In modern terms, Σ^♮_{J,L} is the generalized link (homotopy link) of the J-part in the L-part. The span is the gluing ('recollement') datum that rebuilds the stratified space from the deployed manifolds with corners. The next page adds two points. Σ^♮_{J,L} and its inclusion into Σ_L are intrinsic, defined by local conic retractions in tame topology. The projection to Σ_J, however, needs tubular (or conic) structure and makes sense only in an isotopy category.

Purpose: this serves the 'théorème du déploiement'. A tame stratified space should be equivalent to a combinatorial diagram of manifolds with corners indexed by flags of the stratification poset, with link spans J ← (J,L) → L.
errors: (75): the parenthetical alternative (union over J̄) is struck down by Grothendieck himself ('mais en général c'est différent'). Only the union over J is intended.

The phrase 'pour L = I'\J' conflicts with the NB Σ_L = Σ_{I'} \ Σ_{I'}∩T̊_{J'} and with J' = I'\L. With L = I'\J one gets J' = J and the subtraction in (77) would be vacuous. The intended reading must be a general coideal L ⊂ I'\J, with (76) the special case L = I'\J.

(76) and (78) are colimit formulas asserted 'sauf erreur', with no proof. The gluing maps between the Σ_d (corner/face inclusions) are left implicit. Strictly, the colimit is a union of corner strata glued along common faces and needs a compatible system of tubes (Mather-type control data).
The arrow Σ^♮_{J,L} → Σ_J in (79) is well defined only once tube projections are chosen. The next page concedes this, placing it 'dans une catégorie isotopique convenable'.

ideas.what: Deployment of a stratified space: removing open tubular neighbourhoods of lower strata gives manifolds with corners Σ_J, with corners Σ_d indexed by flags of the stratification poset.
ideas.modern_name: unfolding/unzipping of stratified spaces; resolution into manifolds with corners (blow-up of strata)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom–Mather (control data, 1960s–70s); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka ('unzipping', 2017); Grothendieck's Esquisse as programme
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 ('théorème du déploiement', tame topology) — statement only, no details

ideas.what: The boundary of the tube of Σ_J in Σ_{I'} written as a colimit of corner pieces over flags with initial segment in J and final segment in I'\J.
ideas.modern_name: link of a stratum as a colimit over the subdivision sd(P); exit-path/décollage description
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lurie (HA Appendix A, exit paths); Haine, Douteau (stratified homotopy theory via sd(P)); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka

ideas.what: The generalized link Σ^♮_{J,L} for an ideal J and coideal L, with the span Σ_J ← Σ^♮_{J,L} ↪ Σ_L as gluing data.
ideas.modern_name: homotopy link / holink and recollement span of homotopically stratified sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn (homotopically stratified sets, 1988); Hughes; Weinberger; Miller

ideas.what: The inclusion Σ_{J,L} → Σ_L is intrinsic (from local conic retractions in tame topology), whereas the projection to Σ_J needs extra tubular structure and lives only in an isotopy category.
ideas.modern_name: holink inclusion vs. evaluation-at-start map; well-definedness up to isotopy/homotopy

missed.claim: Grothendieck already writes the links of a stratified space combinatorially as colimits of deployed corner manifolds Σ_d indexed by flags that split as an initial segment in an ideal J followed by a terminal segment in a coideal L. This anticipates the later description of stratified spaces as diagrams over the subdivision category sd(P) (décollages, Haine/Douteau) and AFT's unzipping, at the geometric (tame, manifold-with-corners) level rather than the homotopical one. The link is known in spirit via the Esquisse, but these explicit formulas are not published.
missed.quote: Σ^♮_{J,L} ≃ lim→_{d∈Drap(J∪L)} Σ_d, premiers termes de d dans J, derniers termes dans L
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a concrete point-set/tame model for the sd(P)-indexed décollage of a conically stratified space, with explicit corner gluings. This could inform rigid (non-∞-categorical) models in o-minimal stratified homotopy theory. Its value is mostly historical, since the homotopical version is now known.

deep.surprise_reason: These are working notes on the deployment theorem announced in the Esquisse. The flag-indexed colimit description of links and the link span are, in substance, now standard: Quinn's holinks, AFT unzipping, and Haine/Douteau décollages over sd(P). The page offers an early explicit geometric formulation, but nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: (76) and (78) annotations: 'premiers termes de d sont dans J' (plural, initial segment), not 'premier terme de d est ∈ J'. This matches the splitting (j_1..j_p | l_1..l_q) on the next page.
(77) underbrace: the union index is a lowercase j, i.e. ⋃_{j∈J̄'} Ṫ_j (and second line ⋃_{j∈J'} Ṫ_j), not 'J∈J̄''.
'On pose (pour L = I'\J, ≠ ∅ ...)' is likely 'pour L ⊂ I'\J coïdéal, ≠ ∅'. The illegible part is uncertain.
The struck-out term in (76) is 'Σ_{i_0,i_1,i_2}' with indices marked ∈ J and ∈ I'\J; it is an abandoned explicit example.
The right-margin note in (76) reads '(≃ Σ^♮_{J,I'\J} avec les notations ci-dessous (77))'; the struck-out superscript sits above Σ.
